name: Temperature-dependent photoluminescence spectroscopy in an optical cryostat, 4–300 K
plain_name: Observe a sample changing as its temperature changes

sources.citation: Swidinsky, N., Ellingwood, E., Hucker, J., Skensved, P., Di Stefano, P., Mason, J., Boulay, M., Kemp, A., Schuckman, F., Wang, Y. (2024). Temperature-Dependent Photoluminescence of PEDOT:PSS for use as Transparent Electrodes in the DarkSide-20k Time Projection Chamber. arXiv:2407.08075 [physics.ins-det].

Shyam, I., Singh, R., Akkanaboina, M., Sonawane, A. M., Satheeshkumar, M., Majumder, A., Ekta, Khunte, J. J., Khaire, A., Watanabe, K., Taniguchi, T., Rajaraman, G., Dahiwale, S. S., Kumar, A. (2026). Hexagonal Boron Nitride Spin Defects for Quantum Photonics: Annealing-Free Generation by Krypton Ion Implantation. arXiv:2606.23334 [physics.optics].

reported_conditions.as_printed: borosilicate glass windows in the cryostat shrouds
cold finger, GE varnish, helium exchange gas

requirements.rationale: Swidinsky et al. (2024) recorded spectra from 300 K down to 4 K (±0.1 K); the 4 K base is that paper's choice (Shyam et al. 2026 stop at 20 K). User confirms 4–300 K as the required range.
Excitation and emission pass through cryostat windows (borosilicate in Swidinsky et al.; quartz in Shyam et al.); optical access is intrinsic to photoluminescence in a cryostat.
Swidinsky et al. (2024) used 25 × 25 × 2 mm fused silica substrates mounted on the coldfinger; the cryostat must accept a 25 mm wide sample. Sample size is this paper's choice, confirmed by the user.
Swidinsky et al. (2024) used 25 × 25 × 2 mm fused silica substrates; the cryostat must accept a 25 mm long sample. This paper's choice, confirmed by the user.
Both papers evacuate the sample space before cooling (Swidinsky et al. below 1e-6 mbar; Shyam et al. 1e-5 mbar); an evacuable sample space is required.
Swidinsky et al. (2024) held the sample below 1e-6 mbar (100 uPa). Non-mandatory: Shyam et al. (2026) worked at 1e-5 mbar, so the exact vacuum level is a per-paper choice.

missing_information: cryostat make/model not stated by Swidinsky et al. (cites prior design); Shyam et al. name only 'Lakeshore closed-cycle cryostat'
number of optical windows not stated
lateral flake size not stated by Shyam et al.
thermal load / cooling power not stated
